title: The feature that looked into the future
blurb: As-of reads served newer values and leaked into training.
prompt: A model scored suspiciously well offline and poorly in production, because the feature store served values computed after the training cutoff. The same backfill zero-filled partitions that timed out. Review it, fix it, and prove point-in-time correctness and honest backfills.
aiNote: The draft reads the latest value with no as-of guard, so a backfill against a past cutoff receives features computed later, inflating offline scores, and its offline path zero-fills timed-out partitions, turning infrastructure failures into plausible-looking data.
testIdea: Write a value with a timestamp after the cutoff and assert an as-of read returns the older value or nothing; time out a partition and assert it is reported missing, not zero-filled; bump a version and assert old cached keys are not read for the new version.
followUps: What is the right unit of versioning for a feature?
How would you prove training and serving read identical definitions?
What drift signal would page an engineer versus open a ticket?
